title: Microsoft Copilot: Teach builds multi-week unit plans for educators
summary: The roadmap facts, Teach eligibility and default, and both Integrated Apps paths are supported. Microsoft gives conflicting guidance about whether Integrated Apps blocking also affects Teams; the briefing should acknowledge that discrepancy.

claims.claim: Educators can create structured unit plans spanning multiple lessons or weeks in Teach.

claims.quote: They can customize the plan components to organize connected lesson plans and quizzes across a unit.

claims.where: What's changing
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn describes Teach but does not yet describe its unit-plan behaviour.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teach" "unit plans"; "Teach" "Copilot" "unit". Opened Education AI features and read returned teaching/Copilot results; none documents Teach unit plans.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: No licensing requirement specific to unit plans is published.
claims.quote: Searched: Teach unit plans save storage share quizzes multi week licensing pricing meter; "Teach" "Copilot" "pricing". Read Education AI features and Education Copilot licensing search excerpts; no unit-plan-specific entitlement.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; rationale: cost

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Open questions
claims.claim: Unit-plan storage is not yet documented in the Microsoft material found.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Open questions
claims.claim: How quizzes from a Teach unit plan are shared with students is not yet documented in the Microsoft material found.

claims.where: Why it matters; controls[2].note; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Microsoft directs administrators to disable Teach for selected or all users by removing Copilot Chat access through its Integrated Apps instructions.
claims.quote: To disable Teach for select or all users, remove access Microsoft Copilot Chat following the instructions in step 2 at Remove access to Copilot Chat.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls: first table row
claims.claim: The tenant app block is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Settings > Integrated Apps > Available Apps > app > Block app.
claims.quote:
Select Settings, and then select Integrated Apps.
Select the Available Apps list.
Select an app from the Available Apps list to open the overview pane.
Select Block app.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls: first table row
claims.claim: An API equivalent for blocking the Copilot app itself through Integrated Apps is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot app Integrated Apps block availability specific users Microsoft Graph API PowerShell; "Integrated Apps" "API" "Copilot app". Opened Integrated Apps, Manage Copilot Chat and Package Management overview; package blocking covers agents/tools.

claims.where: controls[0].note; controls[1].note; Scope: Roles
claims.claim: The cited Integrated Apps controls are documented as available only to Global Administrators.
claims.quote: The following controls on the integrated apps portal in the Microsoft 365 Admin Center are only available to Global Admins.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: Blocking the Copilot app through Integrated Apps blocks access tenant-wide in the Copilot app, Outlook and the web, including licensed Copilot users.
claims.quote: If you block the Copilot app using the Integrated app control, you block the Copilot app tenant-wide across the Microsoft Copilot app, Outlook, and the web, including for users assigned a Microsoft 365 Copilot license.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls: second table row
claims.claim: App availability can be scoped at Microsoft 365 admin center > Settings > Integrated Apps > Available Apps > app > Users > Specific users/group in the organization can install.
claims.quote:
Scroll down and select Edit Users or select the Users tab in the overview pane.
Specific users/group in the organization can install means that only the users selected by you are able to install the app on their own from the store and use it in the client.

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance controls: second table row
claims.claim: An API equivalent for setting the Copilot app's Integrated Apps user availability is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot app availability Integrated Apps Microsoft Graph beta API install users groups. Opened Integrated Apps and Package Management overview; read returned Graph/Copilot API excerpts. No Copilot-app availability operation was documented.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: App availability settings do not affect admin-deployed apps.
claims.quote: The availability setting of an app doesn't impact any admin deployed apps. The availability setting only allows you to control which end users can install and use these apps on their own.

claims.where: controls[2].ui and api; Why it matters; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: No Teach-specific or unit-plan-specific switch separate from Copilot Chat is documented on the admin UI or API surfaces.
claims.quote: Searched: Teach unit plans disable admin setting separate Copilot Chat; Teach Copilot disable Microsoft Graph PowerShell settings. Opened Education AI features, Manage Copilot Chat and Package Management overview; no separate Teach control.

claims.where: Governance controls: Integrated Apps changes and Teams
claims.claim: Integrated Apps changes apply to the Copilot app and Outlook, while Copilot Chat in Teams is managed in the Teams admin center.
claims.quote: Any changes made on the integrated apps portal on the Microsoft 365 admin center only impact whether and how a cross application app is surfaced on Outlook and the Microsoft Copilot application. To manage how these apps show up on Teams, use the Teams admin center.
claims.fix: Add: 'Microsoft documentation differs on Teams: the Integrated Apps article says its changes affect only Outlook and the Copilot app, but Manage Copilot Chat says blocking through Integrated Apps also blocks Teams.' Both cited URLs already appear in sources.

claims.where: Governance controls: Copilot app settings
claims.claim: The Copilot app settings in Integrated Apps apply to both Microsoft Copilot and Copilot Chat apps.
claims.quote: On the Integrated Apps page, the CoPilot app settings apply to both Microsoft Copilot and the Copilot Chat apps. Any changes made to this app from the integrated apps portal apply to both.

claims.where: controls[1].governs and note; Governance controls: availability setting
claims.claim: Specific-users availability permits only selected users to self-install and use the app.
claims.quote: Specific users/group in the organization can install means that only the users selected by you are able to install the app on their own from the store and use it in the client. Unselected users are not able to do so.

claims.where: Governance controls: Package Management API
claims.claim: The Package Management API defines a package as an agent or tool such as a plugin, MCP server or skill.
claims.quote: A package represents an agent or a tool, such as a plugin, MCP server, or skill, in the organization catalog.

claims.where: Governance controls: Package Management API
claims.claim: The Package Management API supports blocking packages.
claims.quote: Block, unblock, and reassign ownership of packages.

claims.where: Governance controls: Package Management API
claims.claim: The Package Management overview does not list the Copilot host app itself as a managed package.
claims.quote: The Package Management API enables IT administrators to view and manage agents and tools across your organization.

controlChecks.governs: Whether the Copilot app, and so Teach, is available to anyone in the organisation
Which users can install and use the Copilot app, and so Teach
